name_en: soy-marinated lean tuna — the cure that came before the fatty cuts were prized
summary_ja: マグロの赤身を醤油だれに浸けて締めたもの。冷蔵の手立てがなかった時代に身を持たせる工夫として生まれ、大トロが好まれる今もヅケ専用の仕込みとして受け継がれているという。江戸前寿司の原点にあたる仕事の一つとされる。
summary_en: Lean tuna cured in a soy-based marinade. Born as a way to keep the fish from spoiling before refrigeration existed, it's said to survive today as its own deliberate preparation even now that fattier cuts get the attention — one of the founding techniques of Edomae sushi itself.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: medium-fatty tuna, between lean akami and the richest otoro
summary_ja: マグロの腹身のうち、大トロほど脂が強くない部位。脂と赤身の味がほぼ半々で拮抗するため、脂の重さと赤身の香りを同時に味わえる部位とされる。大トロと赤身の両方の良さを求める客に選ばれてきたという。
summary_en: A cut from a tuna's belly, less richly fatty than otoro. Fat and lean flavor sit close to even here, said to be the part where the weight of the fat and the character of lean tuna can both be tasted at once — chosen by those wanting the best of both cuts.
source_publisher: コトバンク

name_en: the fattiest cut of tuna belly, once dismissed and now the most prized
summary_ja: マグロの腹身のうち、もっとも脂肪が多い部位。かつては足が早く傷みやすいため「猫またぎ」とまで呼ばれたが、冷凍技術の進歩と食生活の変化で今日もっとも珍重される部位になったとされる。切り付けにも独特の配慮がいるという。
summary_en: The fattiest cut from a tuna's belly. Once dismissed as spoiling too fast even for a cat to bother with, it's said to have become, with better freezing and changing tastes, the most prized cut of all today — one that calls for its own particular way of being sliced.
source_publisher: コトバンク

name_en: minced fatty tuna scraps mounded on a rice cup, wrapped in nori
summary_ja: トロの部位を骨についた身ごと叩き刻んだもの。軍艦巻きの定番ネタの一つとされ、切り身では出せない脂と粘りの一体感を楽しむネタだという。骨を無駄にしない工夫から生まれたと伝わる。
summary_en: Fatty tuna scraps, including meat scraped from the bone, minced fine. It's counted among the standard toppings for gunkan-maki, offering a fat-and-stickiness unity a sliced cut can't give — said to have started as a way not to waste meat left on the bone.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: mackerel cured first in salt, then in vinegar
summary_ja: 三枚におろした鯖を塩でしめ、酢に浸けて仕立てたもの。生食に不向きとされる鯖を安全に、かつ身を締めて食べさせるための仕事とされる。江戸前の光り物を代表する一品として扱われてきたという。
summary_en: Mackerel filleted into three pieces, salted, then cured in vinegar. It's the preparation said to make a fish considered unsafe raw both safe to eat and firmer on the tongue — treated as the signature piece among Edomae's oily 'hikarimono' fish.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: sillago given a quick pass of heat on the skin before it's sliced
summary_ja: 皮目に軽く熱を通し、冷水で締めてから開いたキス。淡白な白身に、皮のわずかな旨みと歯ざわりを添えるための仕事とされる。将軍にも献上された江戸の白身の代表格で、小骨の多さも扱いの難しさに数えられるという。
summary_en: Sillago given a quick pass of heat on its skin, then cooled in ice water before being butterflied. It's a way of adding the skin's faint richness and bite to an otherwise very plain white fish — a fish once served daily even to the shogun, and known for its many small bones.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: halfbeak — a slender, silver-bodied fish with a jet-black belly lining
summary_ja: 背は青緑、腹は銀色に輝く細身の魚。腹の中の膜が真っ黒なのが特徴で、下処理でこれを丁寧にこすり落とすかどうかが仕事の分かれ目になるという。旬は春とされ、江戸前の季節を告げるネタの一つとして扱われてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: A slender fish, its back blue-green and its belly a bright silver. Its distinguishing trait is a jet-black lining inside the belly, and whether that's carefully scraped away during prep is said to be where the work shows — a fish said to announce spring at an Edomae counter.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: tiger prawn, boiled straight on a skewer and shelled for nigiri
summary_ja: 活きた車海老を串に沿わせてまっすぐ茹で、殻をむいて握りに仕立てたもの。曲がった尾まで美しい姿を保つための下処理が仕事の中心になるという。活け車海老のまま流通する数少ない海老の一つとされる。
summary_en: A live tiger prawn boiled straight along a skewer, then shelled and shaped for nigiri. Much of the work is said to go into the prep that keeps its body straight and its tail intact right through boiling — one of the few shrimp still commonly sold alive.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: northern shrimp, its raw sweetness building after it's caught
summary_ja: ホッコクアカエビの通称。生きているうちは甘みを感じにくく、水揚げ後にアミノ酸が増えて甘くなるとされる。頭は捨てずに素揚げにされることも多く、身とは別の濃い旨みを持つという。
summary_en: The common name for the northern shrimp. It's said to carry little sweetness while alive, only developing it after landing as amino acids build up — and the head, often fried whole rather than discarded, carries a rich flavor of its own.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: spot prawn, a rarer and richer relative served raw
summary_ja: 甘海老よりも大ぶりで漁獲量が少なく、とろけるような甘みを持つ海老。高価で料亭や高級寿司店以外ではあまり見かけられないとされる。近縁の複数種がまとめてこの名で流通しているという。
summary_en: Larger than the northern shrimp and far less commonly caught, with a melting sweetness of its own. Said to be expensive enough that it rarely turns up outside high-end restaurants and sushi counters, with several related species sold under the same name.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: sea urchin roe mounded in a nori-wrapped rice cup
summary_ja: ウニの生殖巣を酢飯の上にのせ、海苔で囲んで固定したもの。形を保てない素材を軍艦巻きという器に盛る、寿司ならではの解決策とされる。ミョウバン処理の有無が味と品質を左右するという。
summary_en: Sea urchin gonads mounded on vinegared rice, held in place by a band of nori. A sushi-specific solution for serving something that can't otherwise keep its own shape — whether it's alum-treated is said to shape both its taste and quality.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: salmon roe, separated grain by grain, mounded in nori-wrapped rice
summary_ja: サケの卵をひと粒ずつばらしたもの。筋子との違いは薄皮を残しているかどうかとされ、軍艦巻きの形で酢飯の上に盛られる。噛むとプチプチと弾ける食感が最大の持ち味だとされ、色つやも鮮度の目安になるという。
summary_en: Salmon roe separated into individual grains. What sets it apart from unseparated sujiko is said to be whether the thin membrane around each egg is left on, and it's served mounded in gunkan-maki, its popping texture the main draw and its color a guide to freshness.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: squid scored in a fine cross-hatch to make its thick skin easy to bite through
summary_ja: スミイカやアオリイカなどの身に格子状の切れ目を入れる仕事。皮に近い部分に旨みがあるが厚くて噛み切りにくい身を、食べやすくしつつ甘みを引き出すための技とされる。見た目にも美しい飾り包丁の一つという。
summary_en: A technique of scoring squid flesh in a fine cross-hatch. It's meant to make a thick-skinned cut — flavorful near the skin but hard to bite through — easier to eat while drawing out its sweetness, one of sushi's more visually striking knife techniques.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: octopus simmered in a sweet soy broth until it takes on a pale pink blush
summary_ja: 茹でダコをさらに甘辛いたれで煮て、淡い桜色に仕立てたもの。日本ではタコの刺身は生食よりも茹でて用いるのが一般的とされ、そこからさらに手を加えた仕事の一つとされる。吸盤の並びが断面にそのまま残るのも特徴で、コリコリとした歯ごたえも持ち味という。
summary_en: Boiled octopus simmered further in a sweet-savory soy broth until it takes on a pale pink blush. In Japan, octopus for sashimi is generally boiled rather than served raw, and this is one further step of work built on top of that, its suckers still visible across every cut.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: clam simmered in a sweet soy broth and glazed with its own reduced liquid
summary_ja: ハマグリを甘辛い煮汁で煮て、煮詰めたツメを塗って仕立てたもの。生のまま握るのではなく、火を通して味を含ませる江戸前の煮物仕事の一つとされる。俳句では春の季語とされるほど季節感の強い貝で、婚礼や祝いの席にも用いられるという。
summary_en: Clam simmered in a sweet soy broth, then brushed with a glaze reduced from its own cooking liquid. Rather than being served raw, it's cooked and worked into flavor — part of Edomae's tradition of simmered toppings, and a clam tied closely enough to spring to stand as a season word in haiku.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: scallop adductor muscle, sliced thin and served raw for nigiri
summary_ja: ホタテガイの貝柱をそぎ切りにして握りにしたもの。肉厚で淡白ながらほぐれやすく、グリコーゲンに由来する甘みが特徴とされる。生食用と加熱用が区別して流通する地域もあるという。
summary_en: The scallop's adductor muscle, sliced thin and shaped into nigiri. Thick yet mild and easy to pull apart, its sweetness is said to come from stored glycogen — and some regions keep raw-grade scallops separate in distribution from those meant to be cooked.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: ark shell, its flesh reddened by blood carrying iron rather than copper
summary_ja: 血液に鉄を含む色素を持つため身が赤いことからその名がついた貝。コリコリとした食感で高級寿司ネタとされ、市販品にはサルボウガイが代用されることも多いという。鮮度が仕事の質を大きく左右する貝とされる。
summary_en: A clam named for its red flesh, colored by blood that carries an iron-based pigment rather than the copper most mollusks use. Prized for its crisp bite, it's a premium topping often substituted commercially with the smaller ark shell relative sarubō-gai, and freshness shapes the work more than almost anything else.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: the giant water siphon of a gaper clam — a rare topping now often substituted
summary_ja: 貝殻に収まりきらないほど発達した水管を食用にする貝。国産は減少して久しく、今では高級食材の一つとされ、代用として白みると呼ばれる近縁種が多く流通しているという。皮をむく手間が仕事の中心とされる。
summary_en: A clam eaten for its giant siphon, grown too large to fully retreat into its own shell. Domestic supply is said to have thinned for years, making it a premium item now often replaced by a related species sold as 'shiro-miru' — removing its dark skin is said to be the core of the work.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: the fin-moving muscle strip along a flatfish's edge — fatty and prized
summary_ja: ヒラメやカレイの背びれ・尻びれの付け根にある、ひれを動かす筋肉。脂が乗ってコリコリとした食感を持ち、一尾から少量しか取れない部位とされる。かつては高級ネタの代表格だったという。
summary_en: The muscle strip running along a flatfish's back and belly edges, used to move its fins. Fatty and crisp-textured, it's a cut only a small amount of which comes from any one fish — long treated as a flagship premium topping.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: flounder sandwiched between sheets of kelp to draw out extra umami
summary_ja: ヒラメの身を昆布で挟んで寝かせたもの。水分が昆布に吸われて身が締まり、昆布のグルタミン酸が移ることで、刺身とは違う深い味わいになるとされる。冬が旬の「寒ビラメ」に向く仕事という。
summary_en: Flounder fillets sandwiched between sheets of kelp and left to rest. Moisture is drawn into the kelp, firming the flesh, while glutamate from the kelp seeps in for a depth of flavor plain sashimi doesn't have — a technique said to suit winter flounder at its peak.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_ja: 玉子（厚焼き・だし巻き）
name_en: a sweet, sponge-like omelet slice — the topping said to prove a sushi chef's skill
summary_ja: 白身魚や海老のすり身を加えて甘く焼き上げた玉子焼き、あるいは出汁で仕立てただし巻き玉子を切り分けたもの。江戸前寿司では職人の技量を測るネタとされてきたという。コースの最後に選ばれることが多いとされる。
summary_en: A slice of sweet omelet made with white fish or shrimp paste worked into the egg, or a lighter version built on dashi stock. In Edomae sushi, it's said to be the topping used to judge a chef's true skill, and often the last piece served in a meal.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: dried gourd shavings, simmered sweet-savory, rolled into maki
summary_ja: ユウガオの果肉を紐状に剥いて干した保存食を、煮て巻き寿司の具にしたもの。魚を使わない巻物として、握りのネタとは違う立ち位置を持つとされる。栃木県が国内生産のほとんどを占めるという。
summary_en: Strips shaved from the flesh of a bottle gourd and sun-dried into a preserved food, then simmered sweet-savory and rolled into maki. As a roll that uses no fish, it holds a different place from nigiri toppings, and Tochigi Prefecture is said to account for nearly all of Japan's domestic production.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: herring roe, salted or dried into a bundle prized for its crunch
summary_ja: ニシンの卵を塩蔵または乾燥させたもの。プチプチとした歯ざわりが持ち味で、子孫繁栄を祝う縁起物として正月のおせちにも欠かせないとされる。漂白で黄金色に仕上げられ「黄色いダイヤ」とも呼ばれるという。
summary_en: Herring roe, salted or dried into a bundle. Its crackling texture is the point, and it's said to be an indispensable New Year's food symbolizing a wish for many descendants — bleached to a golden color and nicknamed the 'yellow diamond.'
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版

name_en: fish milt, a soft, custard-like organ served raw or lightly seared
summary_ja: 魚の精巣を食材としたもの。タラ、フグ、アンコウなどから取れ、とろりとした独特の食感が持ち味とされる。寿司では軍艦巻きとして供されることが多いという。冬場にしか出回らない季節限定のネタとされる。
summary_en: Fish milt eaten as food — taken from cod, pufferfish, anglerfish, and others — prized for a soft, custard-like texture unlike anything else on the counter. In sushi, it's most often served as gunkan-maki, and only during the winter months.
source_publisher: ウィキペディア日本語版
